memory_update.text: SXT should be the priority underfollowed direct candidate for natural colors and clean-label reformulation inputs; verify Color Group EBIT contribution, natural color mix, and capacity response to synthetic dye regulation.

INGR is a broader clean-label reformulation candidate rather than a natural color pure-play; survival to later layers depends on proving specialty clean-label contribution is material versus commodity starch/sweetener exposure.

BCPC is an adjacent chokepoint hypothesis: flavor/color systems, inclusions, and encapsulation may benefit from reformulation complexity, but product-page evidence must be tied to segment financial materiality.
IFF should be retained as a reference leader for competitive context, but not treated as the main underfollowed alpha candidate because of larger market cap and higher institutional attention.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C pass on adjacent testing, validation, and compliance chokepoints such as food safety/allergen testing providers, because clean-label reformulation can create new verification and recall-risk needs.

node: Natural colors, flavors, extracts, and clean-label reformulation inputs
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a concentrated US-listed universe around natural colors and clean-label reformulation inputs. The highest-purity direct candidate is Sensient Technologies, while Ingredion and Balchem are less obvious mid-cap reformulation suppliers with exposure through clean-label texture, flavor, color, nutrient, and ingredient-system capabilities. International Flavors & Fragrances is included as a larger reference name for competitive context rather than the main underfollowed lane. Key uncertainty: whether synthetic dye and clean-label reformulation demand becomes large enough to move segment EBIT, not just marketing language.
